introduction_markdown:
**General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. Physics 2 (0780), ADVANCED LEVEL, June 2023. Time allowed: three hours.**

Answer ALL questions. Section I is designed to be answered in 1 hour, Section II in 30 minutes and Section III in 1 hour. You are advised to divide your time accordingly. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers. In calculations you must show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage. Calculators and formulae booklet are allowed.

**Structure of the paper.** SECTION I (headed "One hour 30 minutes" on page 2): questions 1 to 5 are compulsory; in question 6 answer EITHER 6 (a), (b) and (c) OR 6 (d), (e) and (f). SECTION II (40 minutes): DATA ANALYSIS, question 7. SECTION III (50 minutes): OPTIONS - answer any two questions from the four options (Option 1: Energy resources and environmental physics, question 8; Option 2: Communication, question 9; Option 3: Electronics, question 10; Option 4: Medical physics, question 11).

No data sheet is printed in the paper: whenever a constant is needed, the model answer states the value it uses.

questions.enonce_markdown: Determine the period of oscillation of the mass;
questions.corrige_markdown:
Take $g = 9.8\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$.

**Spring constant of one spring.** At equilibrium on one spring, $kx = mg$:

$$k = \frac{mg}{x} = \frac{0.8\times9.8}{0.052} = 151\ \mathrm{N\,m^{-1}}\ (150.8)$$

**Two springs side by side (in parallel).** Each spring has the same extension and carries half the weight, so the effective stiffness is

$$k_{\mathrm{eff}} = 2k = 301.5\ \mathrm{N\,m^{-1}}$$

**Period.** The motion is simple harmonic, with $T = 2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{m}{k_{\mathrm{eff}}}}$ (the $4.8\ \mathrm{cm}$ is the amplitude and does not affect the period):

$$T = 2\pi\sqrt{\frac{0.8}{301.5}} = 2\pi\times0.0515 = 0.324\ \mathrm{s}$$

**$T \approx 0.32\ \mathrm{s}$.** (Check: this equals $T = 2\pi\sqrt{x/2g}$, which does not depend on $m$.) The springs are assumed to obey Hooke's law also when compressed, since the highest position of the oscillation is $2.2\ \mathrm{cm}$ above the natural-length position.

questions.enonce_markdown: Sketch a graph to show how the mechanical energy of the mass varies with its displacement from the rest position.
questions.corrige_markdown:
The graph is to be **sketched by the candidate**. Model answer:

Axes: displacement $x$ from the rest (equilibrium) position, from $-4.8\ \mathrm{cm}$ to $+4.8\ \mathrm{cm}$, on the horizontal axis; energy in joules on the vertical axis.

- The **total mechanical energy** is constant (no damping): a **horizontal straight line** at
$$E = \tfrac{1}{2}k_{\mathrm{eff}}A^2 = \tfrac{1}{2}\times301.5\times(0.048)^2 = 0.347\ \mathrm{J} \approx 0.35\ \mathrm{J}$$
from $x = -4.8\ \mathrm{cm}$ to $x = +4.8\ \mathrm{cm}$.
- The **potential energy** (elastic plus gravitational, measured from the rest position) $E_p = \tfrac{1}{2}k_{\mathrm{eff}}x^2$ is a **parabola** with its minimum ($0$) at $x = 0$, rising to $0.35\ \mathrm{J}$ at $x = \pm4.8\ \mathrm{cm}$ where it touches the horizontal line.
- The **kinetic energy** $E_k = E - E_p$ is an **inverted parabola**: maximum $0.35\ \mathrm{J}$ at $x = 0$ (maximum speed $v_{\max} = A\omega = 0.048\times19.4 = 0.93\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$), falling to $0$ at $x = \pm4.8\ \mathrm{cm}$.

At every displacement, $E_k + E_p = 0.35\ \mathrm{J}$.
